messages.subject: Fscores from different objects
parts:
Dear Phil,

Thanks for your quick and previous answer.

I have a new question. Is it possible to estimate factor scores from different models.

Let me explain and contextualize. OECD Pisa 2012 estimates Rasch/partial credit unidimensional model using 480000 observations based on 13 variables to create a home possession index. Additionally, estimates for each country a similar model with 3 variables, which are different for each country ( actually, in the technical report is not clear if they use those variables together or not).

After that, they estimate through WLE factor scores.

I've been trying to come with an idea to replicate the last step but don't know how to merge singleclass objects or extract information from them which could be used for the scores.

Any thoughts?

Thanks a lot,

Lucas

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fscores from different objects
parts:
Hi Lucas,

Try using the mulitpleGroup() function, which allows for grouping-variable structures to be used when fitting a single model. 

Phil

parts:
Hi Phil,

Thanks again for your quick and detailed answers. I´m dealing with IRT by my own here (that means I'm new to IRT, not understanding diverse aspects), so having your advice and mirt is great.

I managed to replicate the model, and estimate fscores, having a correlation of .991

This is how I finally runned:

s<-'F=1-25
CONSTRAINB = (1-13,17-25,a1),(1-13,17-25,d1),(17-25,d2),(17-25,d3),(25,d4),(25,d5)'

group <- as.character(pisa2$CNT)

hom2 = multipleGroup(data = pisa2[,7:31], model=s,group= group,
                       itemtype="gpcm",technical = list(removeEmptyRows=TRUE))

When I tried to calculate M2, this error comes out: 

Error : Multiple Group model will not be identified without proper constraints (groups contain missing data patterns where item responses have been completely omitted or, alternatively, the number of categories within each group is not equal to the total number of categories)
In addition: There were 37 warnings (use warnings() to see them)

I have two questions for this, 1 more conceptual and 1 practical:

1. What is the error message telling me? 

2. Should I apply some kind of invariance? Or some solution as you mentioned before: 

"So, if you know that there is no information from these parameters then you might as well fix them to some constants, say 0 and 1 for the intercepts and slope, because it plays no part in the estimation (regardless of what you set them to the model will fit the same). Unfortunately the syntax doesn't make this very easy in MG models (I'll have to add support for that some time), so you have to do it the old fashioned way with the pars = 'values' approach and passing that data.frame back to the function."

Finally, the last question regarding missing observations and fscores.

3. Is it possible (conceptually, and, practically) to estimate a model with missing data, and calculate scores for all observations?

I've tried to do so, but it comes with an error in the fscores.

Best wishes, sorry for bothering!

Lucas

This is an unfortunate error relating to the computation of the null model for obtaining statistics such as CFI and TLI. Because there are some sparceness issues it's not possible to compute the actual null model. To fix this, pass calcNull=FALSE to M2().

I have two questions for this, 1 more conceptual and 1 practical:

1. What is the error message telling me?

3. Is it possible (conceptually, and, practically) to estimate a model with missing data, and calculate scores for all observations?

I've tried to do so, but it comes with an error in the fscores.
Yes, this is possible. The estimates with more missing data will have larger SEs due to their uncertainty, but that's really the only major consequence. What kind of error are you witnessing?

Best wishes, sorry for bothering!

Lucas
